# Probing and steering biology across Boltz-1s trunk-diffusion boundary

- **Authors**: Piotr Jedryszek, Tongmeng Xie, Adam Winnifrith, Alexander Hasson, Weronika Ślesak, George Wicks, Toby Winnifrith, Oliver M. Crook
- **Venue**: q-bio.QM
- **Published**: 2026-08-11
- **Source**: arxiv
- **Link**: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11475>
- **PDF**: <https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.11475v1>
- **Topics**: reasoning-interpretability
- **Relevance score**: reasoning-interpretability 0.40

## In one line

Probes and steers across the trunk-to-diffusion boundary of an AlphaFold3-class structure predictor, finding that geometry survives the crossing while sequence chemistry is attenuated, and that a strand direction predictive at F1 0.82 steers nothing at all -- with an architectural explanation for why.

## Problem

AlphaFold3-class predictors pair a representational trunk that processes sequence and context with a diffusion module that generates atomic coordinates, and what happens to biological information as it crosses that architectural boundary is not understood. The question matters because the two modules are usually treated as one system, and because interpretability of domain-specific scientific models runs into an evaluation problem general-language work does not: the available annotations are sparse, so a probe can be penalised for being right about residues nobody labelled.

## Contributions

- A characterisation of what survives the trunk-to-diffusion boundary in an AlphaFold3-class predictor: geometry transfers essentially unchanged while sequence chemistry is progressively attenuated along both the layer and the sampling-step axis, consistent with the diffusion module consuming sequence information to compute geometry without re-representing it.
- A within-paper dissociation between decodability and causal use: helix and coil directions steer dose-dependently against a 19-direction matched-norm null, while a strand direction at F1 0.82 and precision above 0.93 produces no measurable change in strand content and instead converts helix into coil.
- An architectural explanation for that dissociation rather than a shrug -- strand pairing lives in the pair representation, information flows from pairs to the single representation but not back, so the intervention site cannot reach it -- supported by the observation that helix and coil, both locally defined, are the pair occupying a single antiparallel axis.
- A demonstration that sparse curated annotations understate what a model represents: identical activations score 0.85 against dense labels and 0.42 against sparse ones for the same concept, with a self-consistency check ruling out structural disagreement, so such scores are lower bounds.
- Evidence that supervised probes outperform the best single sparse-autoencoder latent wherever a label already exists, both in decoding (by 0.13 to 0.35 F1) and in steering reliability, positioning unsupervised dictionaries as hypothesis generators for unlabelled features rather than as replacements.
- Release of the trained trunk and diffusion sparse autoencoders, the per-residue activations, and the analysis code.

## Method

Per-residue activations are taken from the Pairformer trunk and the diffusion module of Boltz-1 and analysed three ways. Linear probes are fitted for two families of concept -- geometry (secondary structure, disorder) and sequence chemistry (amino-acid identity, signal peptides, disulfide-bond annotations, residue-class features) -- with module outputs compared at matched depth, and the diffusion module additionally swept over both its layer axis and the sampling-step axis so that loss of decodability can be attributed to depth or to denoising. Sparse autoencoders are trained on both trunk and diffusion activations and their best single latent per concept is compared against the supervised probe. Causal intervention adds a probe direction to the final trunk single representation -- the state that conditions the diffusion module -- for 97 proteins held out from the 389 on which the direction was fitted, re-runs prediction, and measures the DSSP-assigned share of the target state in the new structure, against a null of 19 matched-norm random directions and with mean predicted confidence tracked to catch degradation. Ablation removes the direction from the trunk, from the diffusion module, and from both. The annotation question is settled by scoring identical trunk activations against dense structural labels and against sparse experimental ones, with a self-consistency check that recomputes the dense labels on Boltz-1's own predicted structure rather than a third-party one.

## Results

The two modules expose different information. From the trunk, both geometry and sequence chemistry are linearly decodable. Across the boundary they diverge: secondary structure transfers essentially unchanged, with helix decodable at F1 about 0.85 uniformly across every diffusion layer and every sampling step including the noisiest, while signal peptide falls from about 0.58 to 0.35 along both axes. The authors read this as the diffusion module consuming sequence information to compute geometry without ever re-representing it. The steering result is the sharpest finding. Helix and coil directions raise their own state dose-dependently against the 19-direction random null with mean confidence stable at about 79, and they lie on a single antiparallel axis (cosine -0.69) that trades one against the other -- driving a single held-out protein each way swaps its helix and coil content. A strand direction that is highly predictive on held-out proteins (F1 0.82, precision at least 0.93) produces no detectable increase in strand content under the identical protocol, and instead converts helix into coil. The ablation completes the picture: removing that direction from the trunk, from the diffusion module, or from both fails to reduce strand content, so the trunk signal is sufficient for decodability and not necessary for generation. The proposed explanation is architectural and testable -- beta-strand pairing is a property of residue pairs carried in the pair representation, information flows from pairs to the single representation but not back, so an intervention on the single representation cannot reach it; consistent with this, helix and coil, which are defined by local contacts, are the pair that occupy the single axis rather than helix and strand. Effects are several-fold larger in low-confidence structures, suggesting the conditioning matters most where the fold is not yet settled. On evaluation, the same concepts on identical activations score 0.85 against dense structural labels and 0.42 against sparse experimental annotations for helix, and 0.83 against 0.33 for strand; recomputing the dense labels on the model's own prediction moves the score by only 0.06 to 0.08, which establishes the gap as under-annotation rather than structural disagreement and makes every sparse-annotation score a lower bound. Supervised probes beat the best single sparse-autoencoder latent by 0.13 to 0.35 F1 wherever a label exists (helix 0.85 against 0.72, strand 0.82 against 0.47) and steer more reliably -- the coil probe moves coil content while the best coil latent does not.

## Limitations

Stated: one AlphaFold3-class model, one main sparse-autoencoder recipe, and a limited set of residue-level labels. Steering is applied only along the secondary-structure axis, so whether the sequence-chemistry concepts the trunk uniquely retains are causally used is untested -- which is notable because those concepts are the paper's own headline about what the trunk holds. Probe folds are grouped by protein but not clustered by sequence identity, with train-test leakage reported as negligible in an appendix. The strand explanation is offered as a hypothesis requiring direct intervention on the pair representation, which was not done. The authors also caution that best-of-many latent selection can inflate scores for rare concepts, which bears on their own sparse-autoencoder comparison. Not stated but worth noticing: the causal claims rest on 97 held-out proteins and one intervention site, and the paper's three methodological recommendations -- specify the readout class, restrict causal conclusions to the site and intervention family tested, control for missing labels -- are exactly the constraints its own strand result forces on it, so they are earned rather than general.

## Why it matters here

- **reasoning-interpretability**: The archive's detection-versus-control principle gets its cleanest instance yet, from a domain with no connection to language reasoning, and with something the language-model instances have mostly lacked: an architectural account of why the gap appears where it does. A strand direction predicts held-out secondary structure at F1 0.82 with precision above 0.93 and moves strand content not at all, while helix and coil directions computed the same way steer dose-dependently against a 19-direction matched-norm null. The explanation is specific and falsifiable -- strand identity is a property of residue pairs living in a representation the intervention site cannot write to, since information flows from pairs to the single representation but not back -- and it makes a prediction the paper then confirms, that the two locally-defined states rather than the two extended ones are the pair sharing a single antiparallel axis. That converts 'decoding is not steering' from a caution into a structural claim about where an intervention can reach, which is the form the archive should want. The ablation strengthens it further: removing the direction from trunk, diffusion or both leaves strand content unchanged, so the trunk signal is sufficient for decodability and not necessary for generation -- sufficiency and necessity coming apart on the same direction in the same model. Two further transfers. The sparse-versus-dense annotation result is the archive's clearest demonstration that a probing score is partly a property of the label set: identical activations give 0.85 against dense labels and 0.42 against sparse ones for the same concept, and the self-consistency check rules out the innocent explanation, so scores against incomplete annotation are lower bounds and cross-paper probe comparisons are only meaningful at matched label density. And the sparse-autoencoder comparison lands where the archive's other evidence points -- supervised probes beat the best single latent by 0.13 to 0.35 F1 and steer more reliably wherever a label exists, leaving dictionaries their real job of surfacing features no annotation vocabulary contains, with the authors noting that best-of-many selection inflates scores for rare concepts. Their three closing recommendations are worth adopting verbatim: name the readout class, restrict causal conclusions to the site and intervention family tested, and control for missing labels.

## Abstract

AlphaFold3-class structure predictors pair a representational trunk, which processes sequence and context, with a diffusion module, which generates atomic coordinates. How biological information changes as it crosses this architectural boundary remains poorly understood. We analyze per-residue activations from the Pairformer trunk and diffusion module of Boltz-1 using linear probes, sparse autoencoders (SAEs), and causal interventions. From the trunk, both geometry (secondary structure, disorder) and sequence chemistry (amino-acid identity, signal peptides, disulfide-bond annotations) are linearly decodable. In the diffusion module, the two diverge. Secondary structure transfers essentially unchanged, whereas sequence chemistry is strongly attenuated. We then test whether decodable directions can steer the model, intervening on the final trunk single representation that conditions the diffusion module. Helix and coil directions change predicted structure dose-dependently against matched-norm random controls, but a beta-strand direction that is highly predictive (F1 =0.82) produces no measurable increase in strand content: linear decodability does not imply causal influence at the site we tested. The same probes also score markedly lower against sparse SwissProt annotations than against dense DSSP labels, because unannotated residues that the model gets right are charged as false positives; such scores are therefore lower bounds. Finally, supervised probes outscore single SAE features wherever a label already exists. We release the trained trunk and diffusion SAEs, Boltz-1 per-residue activations, and the analysis code.
